status: source-reviewed; build and device validation are separate gates

patches.reason: Remove the active debug su permissive declaration without changing allow or neverallow rules.
Do not automatically request a root ADB daemon on recovery startup; preserve explicit authenticated debug root support.
Do not truncate the VTS Android.mk when loading the shell environment; retain the source and its dependency checks.
Require host authentication for recovery even when unlocked/debuggable; exclude trade-in/evaluation auth bypass from the recovery variant while preserving non-recovery behavior.

application_requirements: Apply only inside the separately resolved TWRP source tree, never /work/evolution.
Verify the full selected manifest, each project HEAD and every preimage SHA256 before applying any patch.
Reject unexpected dirty files, path escapes, mismatched base commits, failed context checks or incomplete application.
Verify every postimage SHA256 and preserve a receipt and the source diff; never reset unrelated changes.
verification_requirements: Build the actual recovery and init variants and inspect the generated property files and compile arguments.
Run the unfiltered sepolicy-analyze permissive check on the actual recovery policy and require empty output.
Confirm daemon/main.cpp for adbd_system_api_recovery is compiled with __ANDROID_RECOVERY__ and includes the mandatory recovery authentication branch; inspect all linked authentication inputs.
Require ro.secure=1 and ro.adb.secure=1; confirm actual recovery adbd requires authentication with no trusted key and rejects an unknown key before any log-access claim.
Keep SELinux enforcing; the normal AOSP init property selection is not replaced by these patches.
Review all source changes and inspect the final ramdisk and AVB footer before treating any image as a candidate.
runtime_limitations: No build, boot, authenticated ADB or enforcing device behavior is established by patch metadata or offline tests.
TWRP still reads and writes BCB arguments, can run pending OpenRecoveryScript/startup scripts, and exposes destructive UI and command actions.
The separate minadbd/sideload transport is not covered by the main adbd authentication patch and is not admitted for stage-0 use.
Omitting crypto or userdata fstab entries does not create a write lock; settings, logging, slot/OTA and stock-recovery mutation paths remain outside this narrow patch set.
No phone access or change is authorized by applying this source patch queue.
